candidates.name: Kawakyo
candidates.reason: Two independent firsthand sources (a local Matsue food/lifestyle site and a Hot Pepper diner review) confirm Kawakyo seats only at an 8-10 seat counter, typically booked out roughly a month ahead — it cannot seat this trip's full party of 8 as a single group booking. This supersedes Pass A's earlier, more general "often fully booked" assessment (secondary sources only) with a documented capacity constraint. Matsu-no-Daidokoro Konekkoya's confirmed 24-seat room remains the shipped pick for the full group; Kawakyo is worth the detour for a smaller subset (2-4) wanting the counter experience, ideally booked about a month out.

candidates.reason: not a substitute for Adachi's borrowed-scenery 'living painting' design philosophy — Yuushien is a peony/seasonal-event garden (illuminations, flower displays), a genuinely different genre; good on its own terms, and shares Adachi's fixed-schedule problem (near Yasugi, no slot in this trip's 4 days)

candidates.name: Oki Islands Day Trip
candidates.reason: physically possible as a day trip (~70 min each way via the Rainbow Jet high-speed boat), but it consumes a full day of a 4-day, culture/food-priority trip and leans nature/geopark rather than culture/history; the operator's own guidance confirms rough-weather sailings can be rerouted or cancelled, a real stranding risk for a mobility-constrained group of 8 with no slack day built into the itinerary. Distinct from c-oki-islands-ferry (Pass A's anchor-transport framing of the same islands).

Kamiarizuki (the shrine's lunar-calendar 'month when the gods are present') and the Kamiari-sai rites have fallen entirely within November-December in recent years (2025: Nov 20-Dec 19, per the official Izumo Tourism Association). No official 2026 dates were posted as of this research, but the pattern makes an overlap with the Oct 20-23 trip window very unlikely -- this trip does NOT land in the crowded 'gods gathering' season, contrary to a common assumption about visiting Izumo Taisha in October.

Matsue Castle's busiest hours run roughly 10am-3pm (tour buses and day-trippers cluster then, with the donjon staircase congested); arriving in early morning (8:30-9:30) or from ~4:30pm is noticeably calmer.

Matsue Castle's busiest hours run roughly 10am-3pm (tour buses and day-trippers cluster then, with the donjon staircase congested); arriving in early morning (8:30-9:30) or from ~4:30pm is noticeably calmer.

Peak autumn foliage color at Matsue Castle's Johzan Park typically runs mid-to-late November -- after the Oct 20-23 trip window, so the trip lands in a shoulder period, before both the koyo crowds and Kamiarizuki.

The 'Matsue Lake Line' loop bus runs about every 30 min (full loop ~50 min), Y250/ride or Y700 all-day pass, and covers Matsue Station, Matsue Castle, the Horikawa boat dock, Shiomi Nawate, and Matsue Shinjiko Onsen -- avoids long walks between the day's stops for the 2 low-mobility travelers.

Shiomi Nawate is a ~500m preserved samurai-residence street protected as Matsue's 'traditional beauty district' since 1973, reachable by a 15-min bus from JR Matsue Station -- a walkable, low-key counterpoint to the castle itself.

Tanabe Museum of Art sits inside Shiomi Nawate, adjacent to the Lafcadio Hearn Old Residence, entered through an unassuming long-gate -- a lower-profile setting than the castle or the main tourist street, despite being on the same block.
Reported hours 9:00-17:00, Y700 adult admission, closed Mondays -- sourced only from a secondary reference, not fetched from the museum's own hours page in this pass. Reconfirm before relying on it.
Kizuki, about 3 minutes' walk from Izumo Taisha's main torii, stone-mills its own domestic buckwheat and hand-makes noodles fresh daily.

Tanakaya sits directly across from Izumo Taisha's main entrance and is a tri-colored wariko-soba specialist popular enough that its own site announced a tablet queue system (2026-06-21) after visitors regularly waited outside, including in full summer sun.
Heiwa Soba Honten, about a 10-minute walk from Izumo Taisha with its own parking, is a popular locally-loved shop known for frequent lines even on weekdays.

Kawakyo seats only at a counter, with no tables -- multiple independent diner/guide accounts describe an 8-10 seat counter that is typically booked out roughly a month ahead, making an 8-person group booking impractical as a single party.

Kawakyo seats only at a counter, with no tables -- multiple independent diner/guide accounts describe an 8-10 seat counter that is typically booked out roughly a month ahead, making an 8-person group booking impractical as a single party.

Konekkoya (at the Shinjiko Shijimi-kan, 2F) has a private space seating up to 24 and serves Lake Shinji shijimi and other Shimane specialties -- a party of 8 fits comfortably, and it is on-theme for the Shinjiko-shichimi food priority (lake view, shijimi-focused menu).

Nekkoya (Isemiya-cho) has a completely private room (kanzen kojitsu) seating exactly up to 8 -- an exact-fit alternative if the group wants total separation, though its menu is general Shimane izakaya fare rather than the lake-view shichimi specialty.
Adachi Museum of Art is calmest right at the 9:00 opening; tour-bus arrivals build within about an hour, with crowding particularly around 10am and again around 1pm.
Adachi Museum of Art is calmest right at the 9:00 opening; tour-bus arrivals build within about an hour, with crowding particularly around 10am and again around 1pm.

Yuushien (Daikonshima) is a ~40,000 sqm pond-style landscape garden, not an Adachi-style 'living painting' -- its identity centers on seasonal event programming (peony displays, summer mist, the region's largest autumn/winter illumination); open 9:30-17:00 (last entry 16:30), Y1,000-1,800 adult.

Cars/taxis reach only the Iwami Ginzan Park visitor center; beyond that it is a ~45-min walk one-way to the Ryugenji mine shaft, or a rental e-bike (Y700/2hr) from Daikansho Plaza, or a 6-seat 'Ginzan Cart' (Y500 one-way to the mine). The cart is the only officially confirmed mobility workaround for the 2 low-walking-tolerance travelers, and one cart does not cover a party of 8 in a single trip.

Local bus service (Ishimi Kotsu) from JR Ota-shi Station to Omori/Iwami Ginzan runs on limited frequency -- the operator's own traffic-info page and multiple secondary sources advise checking the round-trip timetable in advance and allowing at least half a day for the site; a taxi stand at Ota-shi Station (Fuji Daiichi Kotsu) is the fallback if a bus is missed. Exact daily bus count could not be confirmed from a live timetable within this pass.
Crossing the Shimane mainland <-> Oki (Saigo) takes ~1 hour by the Rainbow Jet high-speed boat or ~2.5 hours by the regular ferry; a day trip is physically possible via the high-speed boat.

Oki Kisen's own guidance states that in bad weather, departure/arrival locations may change or ports may become inaccessible; the high-speed boat requires seatbelts and the operator recommends seasickness medication in advance. A cancelled or rerouted last sailing has no same-day alternative back to the mainland.

Shimane Prefecture's own transport page frames stable year-round ferry operation as an ongoing goal rather than a guarantee, without disclosing concrete cancellation-rate figures -- consistent with the operator's own weather caveat.

Uzumemeshi -- rice with vegetables, tofu, seafood and wasabi 'buried' beneath it -- is Tsuwano's signature local dish, counted among Japan's 'five great meshi,' still served as everyday local fare rather than a tourist-only novelty.

transport.route: Matsue → Odashi (JR San-in Line) → Iwami Ginzan World Heritage Center / Omori (Iwami Kotsu bus) → Ryugenji Mabu mine entrance (Ginzan Cart)
transport.doorToDoor: Matsue hotel to Ryugenji Mabu mine entrance runs ≈2.5-3.5 hours each way door-to-door once JR, bus, and cart wait times are stacked — this is not a quick side trip.
transport.transferReality: The real bottleneck isn't any single timetable — it's the Ginzan Cart's 6-seat, no-reservation, first-come-first-served design. A party of 8 should expect to split across 2 cart departures or have part of the group walk; nothing about that is stated on the operator's own booking flow because there IS no booking flow. A rental e-bike (¥700/2hr, from Daikansho Plaza) is a confirmed third option for group members who want to move faster than the walk without waiting on a cart cycle.
transport.groupLuggageMobility: The Matsue→Odashi leg carries all trip luggage (this is the intake's stated 'main regional transfer between bases'), which slows platform transfers and rules out a rushed connection. For the 2 low-mobility travelers, the 2.3km/45min walking fallback at the mine is a real exertion cost, not a footnote — factor it into who takes the first cart. Local bus service on the Omori Line itself runs on limited frequency per the operator's own traffic-info page, which recommends allowing at least half a day for the site.
transport.buffer: Arrive Odashi by early-to-mid afternoon to leave enough cart cycles (≈30-40 min apart) for a group split, plus slack before the last practical train.
transport.missedConnection: Missing the last practical Odashi→Matsue train (≈19:24) means either a taxi covering a very long rural distance or an unplanned night in Oda City without a booked room.
transport.nextService: Not confirmed this pass whether a later, slower local service exists after 19:24 — treat 19:24 as the hard deadline until reconfirmed.
transport.lastPracticalReturn: ≈19:24 ex-Odashi (Super Oki service toward Yonago, calling at Matsue)
transport.fallback: A taxi from Odashi to Matsue (long and expensive, not priced this pass) or an unplanned hotel night in Oda City center; a taxi stand at Odashi Station (Fuji Daiichi Kotsu, confirmed via the official traffic-info page) covers the shorter Odashi↔Omori leg if a bus is missed.

transport.route: Matsue (via connecting bus to Shichirui port) → Saigo, Oki Islands, round trip
transport.doorToDoor: Connecting bus from Matsue Station to Shichirui port, then the Rainbow Jet high-speed boat (~1hr) or the larger ferry (~2.5hr) to Saigo.
transport.transferReality: The operator's own guidance states that in bad weather, departure/arrival locations may change or ports may become inaccessible — a real risk given the trip falls in late-October's tail end of typhoon/autumn-storm season. Shimane Prefecture's own transport page frames stable year-round operation as a goal, not a guarantee.
transport.groupLuggageMobility: The high-speed boat requires seatbelts during transit and the operator recommends seasickness medication in advance — not ideal footing for the 2 low-mobility travelers in a swell; the larger, slower ferry is the gentler option if crossing at all.
transport.missedConnection: A cancelled or rerouted return sailing has no same-day alternative — an unplanned overnight on the islands is the practical consequence.
transport.lastPracticalReturn: Not confirmed for a specific date in this pass — check the operator's live timetable close to travel.
transport.fallback: None beyond an unplanned overnight on Oki; no bridge or alternative crossing exists. This is why the islands are evaluated here only as a detour idea (c-oki-islands-day-trip), not part of the shipped itinerary.

disagreements.topic: Ginzan Cart one-way fare to Ryugenji Mabu — the operator's own page states a ¥200-700 range depending on the leg ridden, while a secondary English reference (japan-guide.com) states a flatter ¥400-500
disagreements.investigation: Both are current pages, not stale copies of each other; the range likely reflects different fare legs (short hop vs. full Daikansho→Ryugenji run) that the English source collapsed into one figure. Not worth further budget — the fare is a minor sights-and-activities line item either way and doesn't change any recommendation.
disagreements.resolution: Guide ships the official range (≈¥500 as a representative approx figure) and flags it as approximate rather than picking one source silently.

disagreements.topic: Whether Adachi Museum of Art should ship — Pass A rejected it on itinerary-fit grounds (no open slot in a fixed 4-day, 2-base plan without cutting Izumo Taisha or Iwami Ginzan; also the most generic top-10 pick, cutting against the off-the-beaten-path travel style), while Pass B independently marked the same candidate id shipped, with no reason given.
disagreements.investigation: Pass B's shipped call carried no stated reasoning (candidate.reason: null) and its evidence for Adachi is limited to crowd-timing detail, not an itinerary-fit argument — it never addresses where in the fixed 4 days a ~45-min-each-way Yasugi side trip would go. Pass A's fit analysis is concrete and unrebutted: the schedule is already fully committed (arrival day, Izumo Taisha day, the hard-timed Iwami Ginzan transfer day, and a short departure-day morning).
disagreements.resolution: Rejected for this trip. Pass B's crowd-timing finding (calmest at the 9:00 opening) is retained in the candidate's evidence as a ready-made note for a future, less time-constrained trip that does reach Yasugi.

saturation.note: Combined Pass A (canonical/official) and Pass B (native-language/local/crowd-aware) research converged on the same core shipped set — Izumo Taisha, Matsue Castle, Iwami Ginzan, Tanakaya, Arakiya, Yakumoan, Matsu-no-Daidokoro Konekkoya, Gungendo — with both passes independently reaching the same candidates by different routes (English official pages vs. Japanese resident/editorial sources), which is itself evidence of saturation rather than a coincidence. Pass B added real texture without changing the anchor or the food/culture backbone: Shiomi Nawate and Tanabe Museum of Art now ship as a low-cost add-on to the already-planned Day 1 walk; Matsue Castle crowd timing and the Matsue Lake Line loop bus are woven into Day 1 and Transit; Kawakyo's rejection is now evidence-backed (2 independent firsthand sources) rather than a secondary-source guess, and upgraded to a documented worth-the-detour footnote for smaller subsets; Nekkoya is recorded as the exact-8-seat alternative to Konekkoya. Two candidate-level conflicts surfaced at reconcile (Adachi Museum of Art, Tsuwano) and both resolved to REJECTED on Pass A's unrebutted itinerary-fit grounds — recorded in disagreements/candidate reasons rather than silently dropped. Remaining honest gaps — exact Iwami Ginzan bus frequency, Tanabe Museum's own hours page, whether a slower JR service exists after the 19:24 last practical train — are flagged for a pre-trip recheck rather than guessed, and none is likely to flip which candidates ship: the qualitative picture is stable across two independent research passes.
